bash_execute.description:
Execute any shell command on the Linux server. Stateless: each call is a fresh subprocess, no persistent shell state.

WARNING: bash_execute is NOT subject to MYMCP_PROTECTED_PATHS. It can read or modify any path the service user can access (including audit logs and tokens.json). Untrusted clients should be issued ro tokens, which cannot call this tool.

Defaults: working_dir='/' if omitted; timeout 30s (max 600s, clamped). On timeout, exit_code is -1 and timed_out is true.

edit_file.description: Replace a string in a file. old_string must be unique unless replace_all=true.

glob.description: Find files by glob pattern, e.g. '**/*.py'. Results sorted by mtime desc.

grep.description: Search file contents with regex. Uses ripgrep if installed, else Python fallback.

prepare_download.description:
Mint a one-shot ticket URL for downloading bytes from a server path.

Workflow: this tool RETURNS a ticket URL; it does NOT push to the client. The client must then fetch via:
    curl -o /local/path <ticket_url>
Tickets are single-use and expire (default MYMCP_TRANSFER_DEFAULT_TTL_SEC=300s).

src_path.description: Absolute server path to read from

prepare_upload.description:
Mint a one-shot ticket URL for uploading bytes to a server path.

Workflow: this tool RETURNS a ticket URL; it does NOT pull from the client. The client must then upload via:
    curl -X PUT --data-binary @/local/path <ticket_url>
Tickets are single-use and expire (default MYMCP_TRANSFER_DEFAULT_TTL_SEC=300s).

dest_path.description: Absolute server path to write to

max_bytes.description: Reject upload above this many bytes

overwrite.description: If false, refuse when dest_path exists (default true)

read_file.description: Read a file with line numbers. Supports pagination via offset/limit.

limit.description: Lines to read (default MYMCP_READ_FILE_DEFAULT_LIMIT=2000, max MYMCP_READ_FILE_MAX_LIMIT=50000)

server_overview.description: Return a maintained map of this server's services, apps, data, and recent changes.

write_file.description: Create or overwrite a file. Max 10MB.
